stage1.impression: A night quay with a glowing ring-globe on a black drum, a canal and a block of houses behind. The light and colour are pleasant, but it reads as a clean CG proof, not a photograph. A hard-edged, theatre-like spot pool lights the uniform pavers brighter than the work itself. The houses are one flat dark slab with emissive window cards: no gables, no brick, no rooms behind the glass. The coloured shadow is the one specific idea in the frame. A jury would see a generic render of a ring-sphere somewhere at night, not a specific work on an Amsterdam canal.

blocking_9: The houses across the canal read as Amsterdam: narrow, individually gabled canal houses of varied height and brick colour, not one flat slab with a grid of windows
Lit windows show warm interiors at 2700-3000 K (curtains, lamps, ceilings, depth) with value variation inside each pane, not flat uniform cards (now lum_range under 16 inside a pane, cool b>r)
The globe is the brightest and most saturated thing in the frame: the spot pool on the paving no longer outshines it (now paving median 120 against the globe region's median 25)
The spot pool falls off softly and naturally with no hard elliptical stage-light rim, and the foreground corners sit in shadow
The paving, kerb and water show real material at 1:1: wet or worn stone with gloss variation, rippled water carrying broken coloured reflections of the rims
Atmosphere: a faint halo around the rims and lamps, so the light sits in air
Signs of place and life: a bicycle, a few distant visitors on the route, a bench

defects.what: The hard spot throws a large uniform ellipse with a crisp rim across the whole foreground (paving median 120, falls from 95 to 33 within one profile bin at the left edge), like a stage spotlight; it is the brightest area in the frame
The houses are one flat block with a repeated window grid, no gables, no brick texture, no cornices or hoisting beams; the wall crushes to median 7
The lit windows are flat emissive cards, cool blue-white (r 166, g 176, b 184), uniform inside the pane (lum_range 15), with no interior
Some windows are near white (median 217) while their neighbours are peach; arbitrary on/off pattern, with no curtains or lamps
The water is nearly black (median 8), with smeared vertical reflection columns and little ripple; the globe's colours are not in it
Even, clean CG paving tiles with no wear, joints the same everywhere, no wetness
The plinth reads as a featureless black plastic cylinder with no steel sheen or edge highlight
The rims are thin glowing lines with no bloom or halo in the air; the disc faces read as dark smoked glass rather than clear acrylic
A plain smooth sky gradient with no cloud or city glow
Even added grain over flat surfaces (visible on the window cards) reads as a post filter, not sensor noise

changes.problem: The hard spot floods the foreground with a crisp-edged ellipse brighter than the work, so the frame reads as a stage set and the globe loses hero status.

evidence.measured: paving lum_median 120 against the globe region [150,250,490,580] median 25; the left foreground corner [0,700,150,800] median 119; the profile along y=720-740 falls from 95 to 33 within one bin at the pool's edge

change.setting: the hard spot: power, cone, aim (plus a soft blend on the cone edge)
change.from: 600 W, cone 30 deg, at [0.4, -2.2, 0.0], hard edge
change.to: 300 W, cone 18 deg with a soft blend of about 0.3, aimed at [1.2, -1.6, 0.0] so the pool holds just the coloured shadow and the plinth's foot

changes.expected: A smaller, softer pool that carries the coloured shadow, foreground corners falling to darkness, and the globe as the brightest object; the paving in the pool at about 70-90

changes.problem: The lit windows are cool, flat emissive cards with no interiors, which reads instantly as CG and not as Amsterdam homes at night.

evidence.measured: r 166, g 176, b 184 (cool); lum_range 15 inside the pane; a neighbour [980,130,1020,195] median 217

change.setting: the houses across: the windows' glow, colour and material
change.from: 0.45 lit, glow 0.18, a uniform cool-white emissive
change.to: 0.35 lit, glow 0.10 varied ±40% per window, colour 2400-3000 K, with an interior card per window (a ceiling-lamp gradient, curtains half drawn on some, a dark frame and glazing bars)

changes.expected: Warm, varied windows with depth and gradients inside each pane, none near white

changes.problem: The paving is uniform clean CG tile; wet stone would hold real reflections of the coloured rims and make the frame specific to a winter canal night.

evidence.measured: lum_range 83, an even matte; no reflection of the rims anywhere in the paving

change.from: dry, uniform setts, an even roughness
change.to: damp brick or basalt setts with roughness varied 0.15-0.6 by a noise map, shallow puddles in the joints and near the kerb, a worn, unevenly coloured granite kerb

changes.expected: Broken coloured streaks of the rims and lamp in the paving; more value variation inside the pool

changes.problem: The house fronts and the far quay are crushed to a flat plum mass, so no brick, gables or detail can read.

change.setting: the far quay's fill, and the brick material
change.from: 0.15 W/m2 at 2400 K, a flat dark brick
change.to: 0.5 W/m2 at 2400 K plus 2-3 street lamps across the canal grazing the fronts; a brick texture with mortar joints, varied per house (dark red, brown, near black)

changes.expected: Brick and window frames legible in the shadows, the facade median at about 15-25

changes.problem: The canal is nearly black, with smeared reflection columns, and does not carry the work's colour.

evidence.measured: lum_median 8.1, p95 120; the reflections are vertical smears with no ripple break-up

change.to: a fine wind ripple (about 2-4 cm wavelength) on a slow swell, roughness 0.05, so the window and lamp reflections break into dashes

changes.expected: Broken, shimmering reflections of the windows and lamps across the canal, the water median at about 12-20

changes.problem: There is no air: the rims are thin lines with no halo, which flattens the night.

evidence.measured: the globe region median 24.6 with clip 0.95% on the rims; the background between the rims is unlifted

change.to: haze 0.007 per metre, glow 0.18 (clamp kept at 10)

changes.expected: Soft coloured halos around the rims and the lamps, the globe reading as the brightest and most colourful thing

changes.problem: The quay is empty, a showroom; nothing says canal route or visitors.

evidence.measured: two bollards only; no bicycle, bench or people

change.to: a bicycle chained to the right bollard, a bench at the far left in shadow, 2-3 small figures far down the quay, slightly motion-blurred

changes.expected: Scale and life; the work reads as a festival stop on a real route

changes.problem: The grain is an even overlay that sits visibly on the flat window cards, and the sky is a plain gradient.

evidence.measured: sky median 48, a smooth gradient; uniform grain in the windows at 1:1

change.from: a night gradient at strength 0.12, grain uniform
change.to: an overcast sky at 0.08 with a faint orange city glow low on the horizon; grain weighted to the shadows and lighter in the highlights

changes.expected: A sky that sits behind the houses, about 30-40 median, with photographic noise

out_of_scope.request: Replace the single slab of houses with narrow, individually gabled Amsterdam canal houses (bell, step and neck gables, varied heights, hoisting beams, slight lean)
out_of_scope.why: The card lets only the houses' material finish change, not their geometry; but this is the largest single obstacle to a jury reading the place as Amsterdam

out_of_scope.request: Give the plinth a blackened-steel finish with an edge highlight
out_of_scope.why: The card fixes the low round plinth and does not list its finish as changeable; it now reads as black plastic

out_of_scope.request: Make the disc faces read as clear acrylic rather than dark smoked glass
out_of_scope.why: The globe's design and rim-lit clear faces are fixed; this may be an issue of light, not of the model, and is worth a check against the spec
